subject: Transient burst latency: request to validate SLO breach and proposed remediation
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightcart.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: platform@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout latency spike on 2027-04-09 — impact report

Hi Sofia,

We saw a short but painful latency spike this morning during our peak checkout window (roughly 08:09–08:16 PDT). Symptoms:
- Checkout API median latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s; 5xxs and client-side timeouts reported in our logs.
- ~7% of checkout attempts returned 502/504 or timed out between 08:09:40 and 08:15:12.

I've attached a small CSV with our sample request IDs and timestamps (brightcart_checkout_spike_snippet.csv). Can you confirm whether this maps to any Redwood incident or autoscaler activity on your side, and advise next steps for SLO remediation?

We rely on the 99.95% availability commitment for checkout routing; engineering is requesting an initial read on credit eligibility so procurement can start the internal remediation.

Thanks — we can hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Elena
Elena Torres
Sr. Platform Engineer, BrightCart
elena.torres@brightcart.com

Attachment: brightcart_checkout_spike_snippet.csv (text/csv, 24KB)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightcart.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:32:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spike on 2027-04-09 — impact report

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. We're looking into this now. A couple quick asks that will help us triage and determine SLA eligibility: 

1) Can you share one or two full request IDs and the exact timestamps (UTC preferred) for failed requests so we can correlate with traces?
2) If you have client-side error payloads (502/504) that would help confirm the failure modes.

Proposed mutual action plan:
- We'll pull raw traces and autoscaler logs for 08:00–08:20 PDT and validate whether a regional routing failover or node preemption occurred.
- If we confirm an SLO breach, we will calculate a proportional remedy per the contract and produce a short impact summary + proposed credit within 48 hours.
- We will follow up with a full postmortem (7 business days).

I cc'd Laura and Aditya from Support/Engineering to accelerate the evidence pull. If you'd like to open a HubSpot ticket I can link our artefacts there — otherwise we'll upload traces to the Drive link below and share.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Folks — forwarding BrightCart's report (see below). TL;DR: transient burst ~08:09:40–08:15:12 PDT, ~7% affected. They attached a CSV sample and want a preliminary eligibility read.

What I need from runtime/infra:
- Confirm whether there was any regional routing switch, node preemption, or scale-in loop in us-west-2 during the window.
- Provide request-level trace correlation for the sample IDs (I put the drive link with uploaded traces above).
- Short answer on whether this meets the availability SLO threshold for a pro-rata remedy (contract: 99.95% monthly availability). If yes, provide the calculation inputs we should use for the initial credit estimate.

Attachments we have now: redwood-traces-20270409-08-logs.txt (raw traces), brightcart_checkout_spike_snippet.csv

Please treat as high priority — client already flagged procurement and will expect a remedy path.

— Sofia

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spike on 2027-04-09 — impact report

Hi Elena — thanks again for the report and for being patient while we validated the window. Summary of findings and next steps: 

Summary (initial, technical):
- Confirmed a short-lived latency burst in us-west-2 from 2027-04-09T15:09:40Z to 2027-04-09T15:15:12Z (08:09:40–08:15:12 PDT).
- During that interval ~7% of checkout requests from your account returned 502/504 or timed out; median p50 latency peaked near 1.8s for affected routes.
- Root cause (initial): an autoscaler hot-loop combined with a transient redis shard connection backlog on a small subset of nodes; this produced queueing and elevated tail latency for a limited shard. No region-wide routing failover was triggered.

SLA eligibility / remedy:
- Under our agreement (99.95% monthly availability), the measured impact meets the threshold for a proportional credit because the observed effective availability for the hourly window dips below the SLA target.
- Preliminary credit calculation (pro-rata, pending final telemetry reconciliation): we estimate an initial credit equivalent to 0.18% of your monthly invoice for service usage during April. We'll finalize after you confirm the sample set and we reconcile telemetry.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Immediate: trace bundle + raw logs uploaded (link above) and initial credit estimate provided (this email).
- 48 hours: reconciled request-level evidence and formal credit calculation ready for procurement.
- 7 business days: full postmortem with mitigations and timeline for a permanent fix to autoscaler/job backoff heuristics.

Next steps for BrightCart: please confirm (1) that we should proceed with the formal credit calculation and (2) whether you'd like the credit applied to the upcoming invoice or issued as a billing adjustment after reconciliation. If you want us to open a DocuSign or formal credit note, we can do that as part of the HubSpot ticket (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/BC-1243).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll share the postmortem and action items with the timeline in the next week.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
